questions.question_text: What is the arithmetic mean of the first five prime numbers?
Find the median of the dataset: 101, 102, 106, 109, 110, 112, 115, 117, 120.
questions.step_by_step_solution: N = 9 (odd). Median is at position (9+1)/2 = 5th position. The 5th value is 110.

questions.question_text: Which statistical measure represents equalized 'fair share' distribution?
questions.step_by_step_solution: Arithmetic mean redistributes total quantity equally across all observations.

questions.question_text: Why is a cropped scale (starting above 0) used on the vertical axis of a bar graph?
options: B) To highlight subtle differences among large values
C) To shorten the graph height
questions.correct_answer: B) To highlight subtle differences among large values
questions.step_by_step_solution: Starting baseline above zero zooms in to make small variations in large data clearly visible.

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): Removing an extreme outlier from a dataset significantly shifts the arithmetic mean.
Reason (R): The median is heavily distorted by extreme values because it sums all data points.
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
C) A is true but R is false
D) A is false but R is true
questions.correct_answer: C) A is true but R is false
questions.step_by_step_solution: Assertion A is TRUE. Reason R is FALSE because the median depends on position and is NOT distorted by outliers.

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): Neither the mean nor the median can lie outside the range [minimum, maximum] of a dataset.
Reason (R): Central tendency measures represent interior representative values.
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
B) Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
C) A is true but R is false
D) A is false but R is true
questions.correct_answer: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.step_by_step_solution: Both statements are true and Reason R correctly explains why central measures must fall within the data range.

questions.question_text: The mean mark of 6 students is 18. If one student scoring 8 marks is excluded, find the new mean of the remaining 5 students.
questions.step_by_step_solution:
1) Original sum = 18 × 6 = 108.
2) New sum after excluding 8 = 108 - 8 = 100.
3) New mean = 100 / 5 = 20.
questions.marking_scheme: 1 mark for new sum 100; 1 mark for new mean 20.

questions.question_text: Explain what a Dot Plot is and state two visual features it displays.
questions.step_by_step_solution: A Dot Plot displays discrete data values as stacked dots above a number line. It visually displays: 1) Clusters (dense areas of frequent values), 2) Gaps (empty intervals with no data), and 3) Outliers.
questions.marking_scheme: 1 mark for definition; 1 mark for naming 2 visual features.

questions.question_text: Find the range of daily water usage in liters: 5.6, 8, 3.09, 12.9, 6.5, 12.1, 11.3, 20.5, 7.4.
questions.step_by_step_solution:
1) Minimum value = 3.09 L.
2) Maximum value = 20.5 L.
3) Range = Maximum - Minimum = 20.5 - 3.09 = 17.41 L.
questions.marking_scheme: 1 mark for identifying min and max; 1 mark for range 17.41 L.

questions.question_text:
A teacher recorded test scores for 5 students as: 12, 14, 15, 15, 84.
(a) Calculate the arithmetic mean including the score 84.
(b) Calculate the median.
(c) Recalculate the mean without the outlier 84 and comment on the effect of the outlier.
questions.step_by_step_solution:
(a) Sum = 12 + 14 + 15 + 15 + 84 = 140. Mean = 140 / 5 = 28.
(b) Sorted: 12, 14, 15, 15, 84. N = 5 (odd). Median = 3rd value = 15.
(c) Without 84: Sum = 56. New Mean = 56 / 4 = 14.
Comment: The outlier 84 artificially inflated the mean from 14 to 28, while the median (15) accurately reflected the central group.
questions.marking_scheme: 1 mark for original mean (28); 1 mark for median (15); 1 mark for new mean (14); 1 mark for comment.
